thread.title: Dow set to pull back as Trump says 'highly unlikely' he would hold off on raising China tariffs

author: morningstar.com
title: Dow set to pull back as Trump says 'highly unlikely' he would hold off on raising China tariffs
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch
Apple's shares are down in premarket action after Trump also suggested the possibility of tariffs on iPhones
U.S. stock indexes on Tuesday were set to pull back as remarks from President Donald Trump stoked fresh anxieties about the prospects of a near-term resolution of trade tensions between the U.S. and China.
How are benchmarks performing?
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 57 points, or 0.2%, at 24,540. S&P 500 index futures were 7.65 points, or 0.3%, lower at 2,662, while Nasdaq-100 futures were off 33.25 points at 6,641.75, a decline of 0.5%.
On Monday, the Dow climbed 354.29 points, or 1.5%, to 24,640.24, while the S&P 500 rose 40.89 points, or 1.6%, to 2,673.45. The Nasdaq Composite Index rallied 142.87 points, or 2.1%, to 7,081.85.
What's driving the market?
President Donald Trump told The Wall Street Journal during an interview (https://www.wsj.com/articles/trump-expects-to-move-ahead-with-boost-on-china-tariffs-1543266545?mod=searchresults&page=1&pos=1) published late Monday that it is "highly unlikely" that he would accept Beijing's request to hold off on increasing tariff rates on Chinese goods from the beginning of January 2019, raising some doubts about achieving a detente between the world's two largest economic superpowers when Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping meet on Friday in Buenos Aires. The pair are set to discuss trade on the sidelines of a meeting of the Group of 20 nations.
Trump said that if talks with his Chinese counterpart don't go well that he could put tariffs on the rest of Chinese imports that are currently not subject to duties. "If we don't make a deal, then I'm going to put the $267 billion additional on" at a tariff rate of either 10% or 25%, he told WSJ.
Animosities over trade between the U.S. and China have been among the central concerns for investors recently because an intensification of hostilities could precipitate a slowdown in China and the rest of the world.
Looking ahead, investors will be watching for comments from Federal Reserve No. 2 Richard Clarida, who is scheduled to deliver a speech at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. Clarida recently offered a relatively dovish monetary-policy outlook, saying that he sees 'signs of slowing growth (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-no2-clairida-says-there-are-signs-global-growth-is-slowing-but-doesnt-think-rate-hikes-are-too-rapid-2018-11-16)' and that sluggish expansion in the globe will be factored in the central bank's calculus as it attempts to normalize interest-rate policy.
Read:Stock-market investors cheer Italy, Brexit headlines for a change--but it might not (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/investors-cheerful-about-italy-brexit-for-a-change-2018-11-26)
Opinion: El-Erian: Brexit's overlooked warnings to the rest of the world (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/el-erian-brexits-overlooked-warnings-to-the-rest-of-the-world-2018-11-23)
Which stocks are in focus?
Apple Inc. shares (AAPL) were in focus after Trump said during The Wall Street Journal interview that tariffs could also be placed on iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-falls-after-hours-as-trump-mentions-potential-tariffs-on-iphones-2018-11-26)and laptop computers imported from China if the U.S. decides to put tariffs on additional goods. Shares of Apple were down 1.8% in premarket trade.
United Technologies Corp. (UTX) on Monday announced that it planned on breaking its company in to three parts. Shares were up 1.7% before the opening bell.
Shares of General Motors Co. (GM) looked set to decline on Tuesday after it announced cost-cutting measures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gm-stock-rises-4-on-restructuring-plan-calling-for-layoffs-cost-cutting-2018-11-26) that included layoffs. The car maker's CEO May Barra is expected to speak to President Trump about the layoffs. GM's stock was down 1.2% in premarket trade.
What are strategists saying?
"As for Apple, and the impact from possible tariffs which helped push the shares lower in post market trading, any negative effects are likely to be overstated given that the firm was able to absorb the impact of lifting the ceiling price on its most expensive iPhone model by much more than that with its recent upgrades," wrote Michael Hewson, chief market strategist at CMC Markets UK, in a note.
What data and other Fed speakers are ahead
Case-Shiller house prices for September are due at 9 a.m., and a reading of consumer confidence is set for 10 a.m.
Meanwhile, Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank President Raphael Bostic, Kansas Federal Reserve Bank President Esther George and Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Charles Evans will participate in a panel discussion and Q&A at 2:30 p.m. at the Clearing House Conference in New York.
-Mark DeCambre; 0654ET
